proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a cell \(c\in\mathcal C\), a coordinate \(1\le \ell\le d_c\), and a fold \(1\le f\le L\).  Write \(t=t_{c\ell}\), \(Q=Q_c\), \(G=G_c\), \(\bar Q=\widehat Q_{c,-f}\), and \(\bar G=\widehat G_{c,-f}\), and let \(\mathcal T_{cf}\) be the sigma-field generated by the training observations outside \(\mathcal V_{cf}\).  All assertions about \(\bar Q\) and \(\bar G\) below are conditional on \(\mathcal T_{cf}\).  The inverse-survival metric in Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-estimability} entails that the fitted inverse \(1/\bar G\) is well defined on the required horizon with probability tending to one.  All survival ratios are interpreted with the convention in Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score}.

Put
\[
 N(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\le u,\Delta=1\},
 \qquad
 Y(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\ge u\}.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring}, the tie convention \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{T\le C\}\), and the left-continuous definition \(G(u\mid X)=P(C\ge u\mid X)\) imply
\[
 E\{dN(u)\mid X\}
 =Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X)\Lambda(du\mid X),
 \qquad
 E\{Y(u)\mid X\}
 =Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} excludes an event atom at zero, so the interval \((0,t]\) in the following calculation is exactly the interval used by Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score}.  Taking the conditional expectation of that score and applying Tonelli's theorem separately to its two nonnegative finite-hazard integrals gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E\{\psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)\mid X,\mathcal T_{cf}\}
 =\bar Q(t\mid X)\left[
 1+\int_{(0,t]}
 \frac{Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X)}
 {\bar Q(u\mid X)\bar G(u\mid X)}
 (\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X)
 \right].
\end{aligned}
\]
An integral with respect to \(\bar\Lambda-\Lambda\) denotes the difference of the two finite Stieltjes integrals with the displayed predictable integrand.

Define \(R(u\mid X)=Q(u\mid X)/\bar Q(u\mid X)-1\), as in the symbol \(R_{cf}\).  The product-integral quotient rule is, under the stated convention,
\[
 dR(u\mid X)
 =\frac{Q(u-\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}
 (\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X).
\]
To verify the jump part, the product-integral equations
\(Q(u)=Q(u-)\{1-\Delta\Lambda(u)\}\) and
\(\bar Q(u)=\bar Q(u-)\{1-\Delta\bar\Lambda(u)\}\) give
\[
 \Delta\!\left(\frac Q{\bar Q}\right)(u)
 =\frac{Q(u-)}{\bar Q(u)}
 \{\Delta\bar\Lambda(u)-\Delta\Lambda(u)\};
\]
on the continuous part this is the ordinary quotient rule.  Assumptions~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} and~\ref{ass:learner-origin-normalization} give \(R(0\mid X)=0\).  Integration therefore yields
\[
 Q(t\mid X)=\bar Q(t\mid X)\left[
 1+\int_{(0,t]}
 \frac{Q(u-\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}
 (\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X)
 \right].
\]
Subtracting this identity from the conditional score mean proves the exact remainder formula
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathfrak R_{cf\ell}(X)
 &:=E\{\psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)\mid X,\mathcal T_{cf}\}
       -Q(t\mid X)\\
 &=\bar Q(t\mid X)
 \int_{(0,t]}
 \left\{\frac{G(u\mid X)}{\bar G(u\mid X)}-1\right\}
 dR(u\mid X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus this conditional bias is zero if either fitted nuisance equals its truth; in particular, no first-order event- or censor-nuisance term survives.

Let
\[
 A_{cf\ell}(X)=\sup_{0\le u\le t}
 \left|\frac1{\bar G(u\mid X)}-\frac1{G(u\mid X)}\right|.
\]
Because \(0\le\bar Q(t\mid X)\le1\), \(0\le G(u\mid X)\le1\), and Assumption~\ref{ass:relative-survival-bv} makes \(dR\) a finite signed Stieltjes measure, the preceding identity and the definition of \(V_{cf\ell}\) give
\[
 |\mathfrak R_{cf\ell}(X)|
 \le A_{cf\ell}(X)|dR(\mathord\cdot\mid X)|((0,t])
 =A_{cf\ell}(X)V_{cf\ell}(X).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-estimability} gives
\(\|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(b_K)\), and Assumption~\ref{ass:relative-survival-variation-rate} gives
\(\|V_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\), jointly over the fixed indices.  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz hence proves
\[
 \left|P_c\{\psi_t(\bar Q,\bar G)-\psi_t(Q,G)\}\right|
 \le \|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
      \|V_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 =O_P(a_Kb_K)=o_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
where the final equality is Assumption~\ref{ass:nuisance-product-rate}.  This establishes the asserted conditional second-order remainder.

It remains to bound the cross-fitted empirical term and the fitted influence functions.  For \(0\le u\le t\), define
\[
 r_t(u\mid X)=\frac{Q(t\mid X)}{Q(u\mid X)},
 \qquad
 \bar r_t(u\mid X)=\frac{\bar Q(t\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}.
\]
Both paths are nondecreasing in \(u\), lie in \([0,1]\), and satisfy
\(d\bar r_t(u\mid X)=\bar r_t(u\mid X)\bar\Lambda(du\mid X)\).  Thus, with \(w=t\wedge U\), Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score} is equivalently
\[
 \psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)
 =\bar Q(t\mid X)
 -\mathbf 1\{U\le t,\Delta=1\}
   \frac{\bar r_t(U\mid X)}{\bar G(U\mid X)}
 +\int_{(0,w]}\frac1{\bar G(u\mid X)}\,d\bar r_t(u\mid X).
\]
Set
\[
 D_{Q,cf\ell}(X)=\sup_{0\le u\le t}
 |\bar r_t(u\mid X)-r_t(u\mid X)|.
\]
The event-ratio metric in Assumption~\ref{ass:event-estimability} gives
\(\|D_{Q,cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\), while \(0\le D_{Q,cf\ell}\le1\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-positivity} gives \(1/G\le g^{-1}\); because \(G\) is a survival function, \(1/G\) is nondecreasing and has total variation at most \(g^{-1}-1\) on the horizon.  Splitting the integral difference as
\[
 \int\frac1{\bar G}\,d\bar r_t-\int\frac1G\,dr_t
 =\int\left(\frac1{\bar G}-\frac1G\right)d\bar r_t
  +\int\frac1G\,d(\bar r_t-r_t)
\]
shows that its first term is at most \(A_{cf\ell}(X)\), because the total variation of \(\bar r_t\) is at most one.  Stieltjes integration by parts bounds the absolute value of its second term by the two boundary terms plus
\(D_{Q,cf\ell}(X)\operatorname{TV}(1/G)\), and hence by
\(C_gD_{Q,cf\ell}(X)\) for a finite constant \(C_g\) depending only on \(g\).  The baseline and event terms in the preceding score representation obey the same bound.  Therefore
\[
 \|\psi_t(\bar Q,\bar G)-\psi_t(Q,G)\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le C_g\{\|D_{Q,cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
             +\|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}\}
 =O_P(a_K+b_K)=o_P(1),
\]
where Assumptions~\ref{ass:event-rate-vanishes} and~\ref{ass:censor-rate-vanishes} give the final equality.

Let \(n_{cf}=|\mathcal V_{cf}|\), let \(\mathbb P_{cf}\) be the validation-fold empirical measure when \(n_{cf}>0\), and write \(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}=\psi_t(\mathord\cdot;\bar Q,\bar G)\) and \(\psi_{c\ell}=\psi_t(\mathord\cdot;Q,G)\).  Empty folds contribute zero.  Since the folds partition \(\{1,\ldots,K\}\), Definition~\ref{def:cell-estimator} and the identity \(P_c\psi_{c\ell}=S_c(t)\), obtained above by setting \((\bar Q,\bar G)=(Q,G)\), give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_{c\ell}(O_{ci})\\
 &\quad+\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{n_{cf}}K
 (\mathbb P_{cf}-P_c)(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell})\\
 &\quad+\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{n_{cf}}K
 P_c(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}).
\end{aligned}
\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid}, conditional on \(\mathcal T_{cf}\), the validation observations are independent and identically distributed with law \(P_c\).  Thus the conditional standard deviation of the \(f\)-th weighted empirical term is at most
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{n_{cf}}}{K}
 \|\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le K^{-1/2}o_P(1)=o_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
because \(n_{cf}\le K\).  Conditional Chebyshev's inequality and fixed \(L\) therefore make the entire empirical sum \(o_P(K^{-1/2})\), without requiring equal fold sizes.  The bias sum is \(O_P(a_Kb_K)=o_P(K^{-1/2})\) by the established remainder bound and because its weights sum to one.  Consequently
\[
 \sqrt K\{\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)\}
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_{c\ell}(O_{ci})+o_P(1).
\]

Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} makes the numbers of cells, folds, and coordinates fixed.  A finite union bound makes all preceding rates joint over \(c,f,\ell\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} permits pairing the common within-cell index \(i\) and stacking the cell influences as \(\Phi_i\).  Extracting the target-pre, donor-pre, donor-post, and factual-post blocks gives the stated stacked expansion for \((\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\).

Finally, for observation \(i\) belonging to fold \(f\), define the fitted centered coordinate
\[
 \widehat\phi_{c\ell,i}
 =\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}(O_{ci})-\widehat s_{c\ell}.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment} supplies a finite second moment for \(\phi_{c\ell}\).  The expansion just proved gives
\(|\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)|=o_P(1)\), and the fitted-score bound gives, conditionally fold by fold,
\[
 \|\widehat\phi_{c\ell}-\phi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le \|\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
     +|\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)|
 =o_P(1).
\]
A final finite union bound proves joint foldwise \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistency of all plug-in influence vectors.  This proves every assertion of the lemma.

Stack the fixed collection of cell coordinates in a Euclidean vector \(Z=(y,M,B,s_1)\), vectorizing matrices in a fixed order, and let \(\widehat Z\) be its estimated counterpart.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion}, Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel}, and Assumption~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} give
\[
 \widehat Z-Z=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_i+o_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat Z-Z\|_2=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
The second conclusion follows because Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment} gives finite second moments and the dimension is fixed.

By Assumption~\ref{ass:exact-rank}, \(\sigma_{r+1}(M)=0\), with the convention that this assertion is vacuous when \(r=\min(N_0,T_0)\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:singular-gap} gives \(\sigma_r(M)\ge\kappa>0\).  The singular-value perturbation inequality and \(\|\widehat M-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(K^{-1/2})\) therefore imply
\[
 \Pr\{\sigma_r(\widehat M)>\kappa/2,
          \ \sigma_{r+1}(\widehat M)<\kappa/2\}\longrightarrow1,
\]
again omitting the second inequality in the full-rank case.  Hence, with probability tending to one, \(\widehat M\) lies in the separated rank-\(r\) neighborhood of Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential}.

Applying that lemma's Fr\'echet expansion to Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\theta-\theta
 &=(\widehat y-y)PB
   +y\mathcal L_M(\widehat M-M)B
   +yP(\widehat B-B)+o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \{\Phi_{y,i}PB+y\mathcal L_M(\Phi_{M,i})B+yP\Phi_{B,i}\}
 +o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\theta,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The factual block of Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} is
\[
 \widehat s_1-s_1=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{1,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Stacking the last two displays and using Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} proves
\[
 \sqrt K
 \begin{pmatrix}\widehat\theta-\theta\\ \widehat s_1-s_1\end{pmatrix}
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}+o_P(1).
\]

Each \(\Phi_i\) is centered by the definition of \(\phi_c\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid} and Assumption~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} make the stacked vectors independent and identically distributed over \(i\).  Because the derivative in Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} is a fixed linear map in a fixed dimension, Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment} implies
\(E\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^{2+\nu}<\infty\).  For fixed \(a\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), put \(W_i=a^\top\Phi_{\eta,i}\) and \(\delta=\min(\nu,1)>0\).  Then \(EW_i=0\), \(EW_i^2=a^\top\Omega_\eta a\), and the Taylor bound
\[
 |e^{\mathrm ix}-1-\mathrm ix+x^2/2|
 \le C_\delta |x|^{2+\delta}
\]
near zero, together with a constant bound away from zero, gives
\[
 E\exp(\mathrm iW_i/\sqrt K)
 =1-\frac{a^\top\Omega_\eta a}{2K}+o(K^{-1}).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \left[E\exp\{\mathrm i a^\top\Phi_{\eta,i}/\sqrt K\}\right]^K
 \longrightarrow
 \exp\{-a^\top\Omega_\eta a/2\}.
\]
The right-hand side is the characteristic function of \(\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta)\), is continuous at the origin, and the convergence holds for every \(a\).  Hence
\[
 K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:nondegenerate-covariance} ensures \(\lambda_{\min}(\Omega_\eta)\ge v>0\), so the limit is nondegenerate.

We next establish the plug-in claims.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} gives foldwise \(L_2\)-consistency of each fitted cell-influence block, while its expansion gives
\(\widehat y\to_Py\), \(\widehat M\to_PM\), and \(\widehat B\to_PB\).  On the separated-gap neighborhood, the pseudoinverse \(M\mapsto M_r^+\) and its derivative \(\mathcal L_M\) are continuous by Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential}.  Expanding the difference between the fitted and true expressions in Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence}, every resulting summand is of one of two forms: a bounded-in-probability spectral coefficient times a fitted cell-influence error, or an \(o_P(1)\) spectral-coefficient error times a true cell influence.  Conditional Markov inequalities on validation folds, followed by the finite union bound, and the finite empirical second moments implied by Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment}, therefore give
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2=o_P(1).
\]

Let \(D_i=\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\).  The matrix Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\left\|\widehat\Omega_\eta-
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad\le
 \left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|D_i\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \left[
 \left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 +\left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \right]
 =o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
For completeness, the entrywise weak law for the final empirical second moment follows by truncating each integrable product \(\Phi_{\eta,i,k}\Phi_{\eta,i,m}\), applying Chebyshev's inequality to the bounded truncation, and then sending the truncation level to infinity.  Hence
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top
 \to_P E(\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top)=\Omega_\eta,
\]
and consequently \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\to_P\Omega_\eta\).

Finally, the observed-law map \(yM_r^+B\) is not made causal by definition.  Assumption~\ref{ass:target-pre-span} states the required donor-span representation, and Assumption~\ref{ass:post-transport} states that the target unit's untreated post-treatment survival row equals this transported observed-law functional.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} identifies and estimates every entry of \(y,M,B,s_1\) as a covariate-standardized marginal survival coordinate under Assumptions~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring} and~\ref{ass:censor-positivity}.  Therefore the displayed limit is centered at the untreated causal curve \(\theta\), rather than at the marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-target.  This proves the theorem.

Let \(\Omega_\theta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\) be the counterfactual \(J\times J\) principal blocks of \(\Omega_\eta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\).  Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} gives
\(\widehat\Omega_\theta\to_P\Omega_\theta\).  If \(x\in\mathbb R^J\), embed it as \((x^\top,0^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^{2J}\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:nondegenerate-covariance} then gives
\[
 x^\top\Omega_\theta x\ge v\|x\|_2^2.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\Omega_\theta)\ge v,
 \qquad
 \sigma_j^2:=(\Omega_\theta)_{jj}\ge v,
 \qquad
 \widehat\sigma_j\to_P\sigma_j>0
\]
for all \(1\le j\le J\).  Thus every division in Definition~\ref{def:multiplier-band} is well defined with probability tending to one.

Conditionally on the sample, independence and Gaussianity of the multipliers \(\xi_i\) imply that
\[
 Z_K^*=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\xi_i\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i}
\]
is exactly centered Gaussian with covariance \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\).  Its studentized covariance is
\[
 \widehat R_K
 =\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}
  \widehat\Omega_\theta
  \operatorname{diag}(\widehat\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}
 \to_P
 R:=\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}
  \Omega_\theta
  \operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}.
\]
The matrix \(R\) is positive definite.  If \(Z\sim\mathcal N_J(0,R)\), then \(Z\) has a Lebesgue density that is positive everywhere.  Hence the boundary of each cube \([-x,x]^J\) has probability zero, and every nonempty shell \([-x_2,x_2]^J\setminus[-x_1,x_1]^J\), with \(0\le x_1<x_2\), has positive probability.  It follows that the distribution function of \(\max_j|Z_j|\) is continuous and strictly increasing on its nontrivial range.  Continuity of matrix square roots gives a coupling \(\widehat R_K^{1/2}\varepsilon\to R^{1/2}\varepsilon\) in probability for \(\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N_J(0,I_J)\), conditionally along every subsequence on which \(\widehat R_K\to R\).  Therefore the conditional distribution functions converge at every point, and strict continuity at the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile gives
\[
 c_{1-\alpha}^\star\to_P c_{1-\alpha},
 \qquad
 \Pr\{\max_{1\le j\le J}|Z_j|\le c_{1-\alpha}\}=1-\alpha.
\]

On the sampling side, Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit}, covariance consistency, and the continuous-mapping theorem give
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le J}
 \left|\frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j)}{\widehat\sigma_j}\right|
 \rightsquigarrow
 \max_{1\le j\le J}|Z_j|.
\]
Combining this convergence with \(c_{1-\alpha}^\star\to_Pc_{1-\alpha}\) and continuity of the limiting distribution at \(c_{1-\alpha}\) yields
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\theta_j\in
 \left[\widehat\theta_j\pm
 c_{1-\alpha}^\star\widehat\sigma_j/\sqrt K\right]
 \text{ for every }1\le j\le J\right\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} is used here to keep \(J\) fixed; this is not a growing-grid approximation.

For the scalar target, Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map}, the definition \(\tau_R=q^\top(s_1-\theta)\), and Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)
 &=q^\top\sqrt K\{(\widehat s_1-s_1)-(\widehat\theta-\theta)\}\\
 &=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K
 q^\top(\Phi_{1,i}-\Phi_{\theta,i})+o_P(1)\\
 &=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\tau,i}+o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(a=(-q^\top,q^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^{2J}\).  Since the declared quadrature vector satisfies \(q\in(0,\infty)^J\), it is nonzero.  Assumption~\ref{ass:nondegenerate-covariance} therefore gives the strictly positive variance
\[
 V_R=E\Phi_{\tau,i}^2
 =a^\top\Omega_\eta a
 \ge v\|a\|_2^2
 =2v\|q\|_2^2>0.
\]
The empirical \(L_2\)-consistency in Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\left|\widehat V_R-K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\tau,i}^2\right|\\
 &\quad\le \|q\|_2^2
 \left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \| (\widehat\Phi_{1,i}-\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i})
     -(\Phi_{1,i}-\Phi_{\theta,i})\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &\qquad\times
 \left[
 \left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \|\widehat\Phi_{1,i}-\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i}\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 +\left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \|\Phi_{1,i}-\Phi_{\theta,i}\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \right]
 =o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
The entrywise weak-law argument in Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} gives
\(K^{-1}\sum_i\Phi_{\tau,i}^2\to_PV_R\), so \(\widehat V_R\to_PV_R>0\).  The scalar projection of the joint Gaussian limit and Slutsky's theorem now yield
\[
 \frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)}{\sqrt{\widehat V_R}}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
It follows that
\[
 \left[\widehat\tau_R-z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_R/K},
       \widehat\tau_R+z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_R/K}\right]
\]
has limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  This final statement concerns exactly the declared grid functional \(q^\top(s_1-\theta)\); it does not assert identification or coverage for a continuous-time RMST integral.  The theorem follows.
